title: ALARB: An Arabic Legal Argument Reasoning Benchmark
authors: Harethah Abu Shairah; Somayah AlHarbi; Abdulaziz AlHussein; Sameer Alsabea; Omar Shaqaqi; Hebah AlShamlan; Omar Knio; George Turkiyyah
task_description: Verdict prediction; completion of multistep legal reasoning chains; and identification of relevant regulations from case facts.
inputs: Over 13K Saudi commercial court cases with facts, court reasoning, verdict, and cited regulatory clauses.
outputs_or_labels: Verdict; reasoning-chain completion; relevant regulations; cited clauses.
pipeline_gap_filled: Attributed claims -> argument/proof skeleton -> provenance-preserving evaluation
artifact_access_status: Paper and ACL PDF accessible; dataset/code release is asserted by paper but artifact URL was not independently resolved in this pass.
license_status: ACL paper CC BY 4.0; dataset/code license not independently verified.
evidence_basis: ACL Anthology abstract and paper record state corpus size, fields, and tasks.
limitations: Saudi positive-law cases are not classical qiyas or kalam; court reasoning may not expose tradition-specific warrants.
why_relevant: Best current Arabic benchmark for explicit reasoning chains plus cited authorities; useful adapter for Islamic-law argument evaluation.

title: NYUAD at QIAS Shared Task: Benchmarking the Legal Reasoning of LLMs in Arabic Islamic Inheritance Cases
task_description: Structured Islamic inheritance reasoning from natural-language cases: identify heirs, apply blocking rules, assign shares, detect adjustments, and produce final distribution.
inputs: Arabic inheritance cases; the shared-task description identifies MAWARITH as 12,500 cases with intermediate reasoning steps and final answers.
outputs_or_labels: Intermediate stages and final inheritance distribution; MIR-E-style multistep evaluation is described for QIAS.
pipeline_gap_filled: Cross-tradition argument form -> executable proof/dependency skeleton -> strength evaluation
artifact_access_status: Scholarly task paper and PDF accessible; underlying MAWARITH artifact URL not independently resolved.
license_status: Paper CC BY 4.0; dataset license not independently verified.
evidence_basis: ACL Anthology task record and 2026 OSACT event description.
limitations: Inheritance calculation is a rule-governed fiqh task, not a general qiyas corpus or open-ended disputation benchmark.
why_relevant: Closest verified executable Islamic reasoning task with explicit intermediate states; directly supports stage-level scoring.

title: Munazarat 1.0: A Corpus of Arabic Competitive Debates
authors: Mohammad M. Khader; AbdulGabbar Al-Sharafi; Mohamad Hamza Al-Sioufy; Wajdi Zaghouani; Ali Al-Zawqari
task_description: Speech corpus for Arabic competitive debates intended for argument-mining and rhetoric analysis.
inputs: Approximately 50 hours from 73 QatarDebate-recognized debates; machine transcription reviewed by three native Arabic speakers; rich debate metadata.
outputs_or_labels: Debate turns and metadata; paper does not report tradition-specific argument-role labels.
pipeline_gap_filled: Disputation retrieval -> dialogue/argument extraction -> dialectical structure
artifact_access_status: Paper/PDF accessible; corpus distribution endpoint not independently verified.
license_status: Dataset license not stated in opened ACL record.
evidence_basis: ACL abstract and PDF describe size, provenance, review process, and intended argument-mining use.
limitations: Modern competitive debates are not medieval munazarat or scholastic texts; no explicit premise/objection/reply annotation reported.
why_relevant: A realistic Arabic disputation source for building and testing dialectical segmentation before historical transfer.

title: ArabLegalEval: A Multitask Benchmark for Assessing Arabic Legal Knowledge in Large Language Models
authors: Faris Hijazi; Somayah AlHarbi; Abdulaziz AlHussein; Harethah Abu Shairah; Reem AlZahrani; Hebah AlShamlan; Omar Knio; George Turkiyyah
task_description: Multitask Arabic legal evaluation including legal MCQs, Najiz QA, contract QA, privacy-policy entailment, and other legal knowledge/reasoning tasks.
inputs: Saudi legal documents, synthesized questions, translated or generated task instances, and answer contexts.
outputs_or_labels: Task-specific answers and entailment/QA outcomes; no explicit historical argument-form labels.
pipeline_gap_filled: Grounding/provenance controls and Arabic legal reasoning control suite
artifact_access_status: ACL paper and linked code repository are public; exact data files/license require separate artifact verification.
license_status: Code repository license/data terms not independently verified.
evidence_basis: ACL record states task composition, sources, automatic validation workflow, and code release.
limitations: Mostly legal knowledge/QA rather than recoverable argument skeletons; contemporary Saudi law.
why_relevant: Useful control suite for Arabic retrieval, citation grounding, and legal reasoning without claiming tradition-specific logic coverage.

title: A Database of Mishnaic Disputes
task_description: Structured database of Mishnaic arguments and disputes, including participants, direction of opinions, and which Tanna prevails.
inputs: Manual coding of every argument in the Mishnah; Arguments.csv and Disputes.csv are released in the repository.
outputs_or_labels: Argument/dispute records; participant positions; strict/lenient orientation; winner under Maimonidean rule.
pipeline_gap_filled: Cross-tradition argument form -> disputation structure -> outcome/provenance graph
artifact_access_status: Scholarly paper and public GitHub database accessible; files visibly available in repository.
license_status: Repository license not independently verified in this pass.
evidence_basis: JSIJ paper and repository README describe coding scope, schema, and downloadable files.
limitations: Mishnaic disputes are not a complete Talmudic dialectic; coding is interpretive and outcome-centric rather than premise-span aligned.
why_relevant: Strongest found Jewish/Hebrew tradition resource with explicit disagreement records and inspectable argument artifacts.

title: A graph database of scholastic relationships in the Babylonian Talmud
task_description: Named-entity and relation extraction over aligned Hebrew/English Talmud text; graph construction for citation, inquiry, objection, retort, support, disagreement, and related interactions.
inputs: Entire Talmud processed; approximately 157,000 named-entity occurrences, about 5,000 scholastic nodes, and 21,924 interactions; small-tracate evaluation reported.
outputs_or_labels: Typed interaction edges and scholar nodes; precision/recall for entity stages; page-level provenance.
pipeline_gap_filled: Argument/disputation graph extraction -> authority attribution -> provenance
artifact_access_status: Scholarly article accessible; online presentation is linked by article but data-download/license not independently verified.
evidence_basis: Oxford abstract/full page reports graph construction, interaction types, counts, and evaluation results.
limitations: Focuses on scholars and relations, not full premise/conclusion semantics or formal validity.
why_relevant: High-value Jewish/Aramaic dialectical graph adapter with explicit objection/retort/support labels and source-page links.

title: Index Thomisticus Treebank
venue: University of Milan / University of Tübingen corpus project
task_description: Dependency-based syntactic annotation of selected Thomas Aquinas texts, enabling parsing and structured analysis of medieval Latin scholastic prose.
inputs: Approximately 60,000 tokens from the roughly 11-million-token Index Thomisticus corpus; CoNLL distribution is documented.
outputs_or_labels: Dependency trees and morphosyntactic layers; no direct objection/reply labels.
pipeline_gap_filled: Authentic medieval Latin source layer -> structured representation -> provenance-preserving extraction
artifact_access_status: Official project and University of Tübingen repository pages accessible; CoNLL artifact availability documented.
license_status: Artifact license should be checked at download time.
evidence_basis: University and repository records describe corpus scope, annotation type, format, and source corpus.
limitations: Syntactic treebank is not an argument-form benchmark; Thomas Aquinas coverage is selective.
why_relevant: Practical medieval Latin substrate for scholastic argument segmentation and alignment with *quaestio* structures.

title: Open Islamicate Texts Initiative
task_description: Machine-actionable corpus and metadata/versioning infrastructure for premodern Arabic and Islamicate texts.
inputs: Premodern Arabic/Islamicate texts with normalization, metadata, versioning, and machine-readable organization across genres.
outputs_or_labels: Texts, metadata, author/work identifiers, and versioned corpus files; not argument labels.
pipeline_gap_filled: Authentic source text -> provenance/attribution -> corpus construction for qiyas/fiqh/kalām modules
artifact_access_status: Official project documentation and repository are public; corpus subsets require separate download/license audit.
license_status: Mixed corpus licensing and edition rights vary; not treated as one uniform license.
evidence_basis: Project documentation and local scholarly review identify corpus purpose and limitations.
limitations: Infrastructure is not a benchmark and does not provide validated argument annotations.
why_relevant: Primary enabling resource for building historically grounded Islamic and Arabic-Jewish argument-form benchmarks.

title: Cubical Type Theoretic Navya-Nyaya
task_description: Executable formalization of Navya-Nyaya technical language with worked encodings and internal theorem checks.
inputs: Sanskrit philosophical passages and formal signatures for relation, delimitor, absence, pervasion, identity, and qualifier-qualified structure.
outputs_or_labels: Formal encodings, typed relations, theorem/check traces, and worked examples.
pipeline_gap_filled: Nyaya argument form -> typed executable IR -> proof/check trace
artifact_access_status: Preprint and implementation sketch are publicly described; full artifact access and exact code status need verification.
evidence_basis: Local scholarly summary and arXiv record identify formal constructs, worked encodings, and Agda-oriented implementation.
limitations: Frontier preprint; not a benchmark with standardized train/dev/test or model baselines.
why_relevant: Best found formal/executable precedent for Nyaya-specific typed relations and proof traces; use as schema/adapter rather than established benchmark.

title: Pramana: Fine-Tuning Large Language Models for Epistemic Reasoning through Navya-Nyaya
authors: Authors as listed on arXiv record
artifact_url: https://huggingface.co (linked from paper; exact collection not independently resolved)
task_description: Fine-tuning/evaluation on 55 Nyaya-structured logical problems covering constraint satisfaction, Boolean SAT, and multistep deduction.
inputs: 55 structured problems framed through Navya-Nyaya epistemological methodology.
outputs_or_labels: Problem answers and reasoning traces; paper claims released models, datasets, and training infrastructure.
pipeline_gap_filled: Nyaya-specific executable task -> multistep reasoning evaluation
artifact_access_status: ArXiv record accessible; claimed Hugging Face artifact was not independently resolved in this pass.
evidence_basis: ArXiv search result states task count, problem families, and release claim.
limitations: Small synthetic set; historical fidelity and annotation provenance need expert audit; no evidence yet of original Sanskrit textual grounding.
why_relevant: Only directly named Nyaya benchmark-like task found; valuable but should be treated as provisional until artifact and provenance are verified.

title: ORCHID: A Chinese Debate Corpus for Target-Independent Stance Detection and Argumentative Dialogue Summarization
authors: Authors as listed on arXiv record
task_description: Chinese debate corpus for stance detection and argumentative dialogue summarization.
inputs: Chinese debate/dialogue text; public dataset details require artifact verification.
outputs_or_labels: Stance labels and argumentative summaries as described by paper.
artifact_access_status: ArXiv record accessible; artifact URL/license not independently resolved.
evidence_basis: ArXiv abstract identifies corpus and tasks.
limitations: Not Mohist or historically situated; target-independent stance is weaker than formal argument-form annotation.
why_relevant: Useful Chinese-language control for cross-lingual argumentative dialogue while preserving a clear non-Western language setting.

title: Crowdsourcing Argumentation Structures in Chinese Hotel Reviews
authors: Authors as listed on arXiv record
task_description: Crowdsourced annotation of argument components and relations in Chinese reviews.
inputs: 4,814 argument-component annotations and 411 argument-relation annotations in Chinese hotel reviews.
outputs_or_labels: Argument components and relations; annotation quality compared with other argument corpora.
artifact_access_status: ArXiv record accessible; dataset/code access and license not independently resolved.
evidence_basis: ArXiv abstract reports annotation counts and task type.
limitations: Domain is commercial reviews; no Mohist terminology, historical context, or dialectical tradition.
why_relevant: Control for Chinese argument mining; should not be presented as a Mohist benchmark.

title: Aristotelian Syntax from a Computational–Combinatorial Point of View
task_description: Rule-based computational reconstruction of Aristotelian syllogistic using reduction relations and computer-assisted analysis.
inputs: Aristotelian syllogistic forms and reduction rules.
outputs_or_labels: Derivation/reduction traces and formal properties of the rule system.
pipeline_gap_filled: Aristotelian argument form -> executable derivation/proof trace
artifact_access_status: Publisher page and author PDF identified; software/artifact availability not independently verified.
license_status: Paper/PDF access does not establish software license.
evidence_basis: Local scholarly summary plus Oxford bibliographic record describe reduction system and computer analysis.
limitations: Not a natural-language benchmark; modern formal reconstruction can diverge from historical interpretation.
why_relevant: Reusable blueprint for an Aristotelian module and proof-trace evaluator, but not a drop-in corpus benchmark.
